01Computer Fundamentals · Guide 01 / 12

Paging vs Segmentation

Computer ki memory me programs kahan rehte hain? Paging aur Segmentation memory ko manage karne ke do tareeke hain — ek memory ko barabar ke tukdon me kaat ta hai, doosra use matlab ke hisaab se baant ta hai. OS interviews me ye comparison pakka aata hai.

1. Paging vs Segmentation — kitaab wali kahani

Paging: Socho ek bahut badi kitaab hai. Tum use barabar ke pages me kaat dete ho — har page 4KB ka. Koi page kahin bhi rakha ja sakta hai — almari ke kisi bhi khaane me. Page number se pata chalta hai kaunsa page kahan hai.

Segmentation: Is baar tum kitaab ko chapters me baant te ho — Chapter 1 (pehchan), Chapter 2 (kahani), Chapter 3 (ant). Har chapter ka size alag hai, kyunki har chapter ka matlab alag hai. Chapter ka naam + uske andar ki line se pata chalta hai kya kahan hai.

Ek line me: Paging = memory ko fixed-size blocks (pages) me baantna. Segmentation = memory ko logical parts (segments — code, data, stack) me baantna, har ek ka size alag.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Paging — fixed-size pages

Paging me logical memory ko fixed-size pages me aur physical memory ko same size ke frames me baanta jata hai (aam taur pe 4KB). Har page kisi bhi khaali frame me ja sakta hai — continuous hone ki zaroorat nahi.

Page table batati hai kaunsa page kis frame me hai. CPU har address ko translate karta hai: logical address = page number + offset → physical address = frame number + offset. Ye translation MMU (Memory Management Unit) hardware karta hai, aur TLB (cache) use fast banata hai.

Plus: External fragmentation nahi hoti (har page kahin bhi fit ho jata hai). Minus: Internal fragmentation hoti hai (aakhri page aadha khaali reh jaye to), aur page table badi ho sakti hai.

Segmentation — logical parts

Segmentation me program ko uske logical hisso me baanta jata hai: code segment, data segment, stack segment, heap segment. Har segment ka size alag hota hai — code 100KB, stack 8KB, data 50KB.

Address hota hai: segment number + offset. Segment table me har segment ka base address aur limit hoti hai. CPU check karta hai: offset limit se zyada to nahi? Zyada ho to segmentation fault — wahi famous 'segfault'!

Plus: Logical structure milti hai — code aur data alag, protection alag-alag lag sakti hai (code ko read-only banao). Minus: External fragmentation hoti hai — segments alag size ke hain, to beech me chhote khaali gaps ban jate hain jinme kuch fit nahi hota.

Fragmentation — dono ki kamzori

Internal fragmentation (Paging): Page fixed 4KB ka hai, program ko 4.5KB chahiye — 2 pages milenge (8KB), 3.5KB waste. Har process ka aakhri page aadha khaali rehta hai.

External fragmentation (Segmentation): Segments alag-alag size ke aate-jaate rehte hain — memory me chhote-chhote khaali tukde ban jate hain, jinme koi segment fit nahi hota, halanki total khaali jagah kaafi hai. Isse compaction (saara data ek taraf sarakana) se fix karte hain — par wo slow hai.

Solution: Modern OS paged segmentation use karte hain — pehle segments me baanto (logical), phir har segment ko pages me kaato (physical). Dono ke fayde, dono ki kamzoriyan kam.

Aaj kya use hota hai?

Aaj ke OS (Linux, Windows, macOS) paging ko base banate hain, segmentation ko limited tareeke se use karte hain. x86-64 me segmentation lagbhag band hai — sirf kuch khaas kaam (TLS, security) ke liye bachi hai.

Virtual memory: Paging ki wajah se har process ko lagta hai uske paas poori memory hai — pages disk (swap) pe bhi ja sakte hain. Demand paging: Page tabhi load karo jab zaroorat ho — program fast start hota hai.

Page fault: Jab CPU kisi page ko maange jo memory me nahi hai (disk pe hai) — OS use disk se laata hai. Zyada page faults = system slow (thrashing).

3. Side-by-side comparison

CheezPagingSegmentation
DivisionFixed-size pages (4KB)Variable-size segments (logical)
Based onPhysical divisionLogical division (code/data/stack)
AddressPage number + offsetSegment number + offset
TablePage tableSegment table (base + limit)
FragmentationInternalExternal
ProtectionPer-page ( mushkil)Per-segment (aasan)
SharingMushkilAasan (code segment share karo)

4. Try karo — memory allocate karo

Ek program ko memory chahiye. Pehle paging se, phir segmentation se allocate karo — aur dekho fragmentation kahan hoti hai.

  1. 1. Paging — program load karo
    • → Program size: 10KB, page size: 4KB → 3 pages chahiye (12KB)
    • → Page 0 → Frame 5, Page 1 → Frame 2, Page 2 → Frame 9
    • → Pages alag-alag frames me hain — continuous hone ki zaroorat nahi ✓
    • → Page table bani: {0:5, 1:2, 2:9}
    • → Waste: 2KB (aakhri page aadha khaali) — internal fragmentation
    • → CPU address translate karta hai: page 1, offset 100 → frame 2, offset 100
  2. 2. Segmentation — program load karo
    • → Program: Code 6KB, Data 3KB, Stack 1KB — 3 segments
    • → Segment table: Code → base 1000, limit 6KB; Data → base 5000, limit 3KB; Stack → base 9000, limit 1KB
    • → Address: (segment=Data, offset=200) → 5000+200 = 5200 ✓
    • → Offset limit se zyada hua to SEGFAULT! (offset 4000, limit 3KB ✗)
    • → Protection: Code segment ko read-only banaya — koi badal nahi sakta ✓
  3. 3. External fragmentation dekho
    • → Segmentation me: segments aaye aur gaye — memory me gaps ban gaye
    • → Khaali jagah: 2KB + 3KB + 1KB = 6KB total
    • → Naya segment 5KB ka aaya — koi ek gap 5KB ka nahi! ✗
    • → Total jagah kaafi hai, par ek tukde me nahi — EXTERNAL FRAGMENTATION
    • → Fix: compaction — saara data ek taraf sarakao (slow, par kaam karta hai)
  4. 4. Page fault dekho
    • → Program ne page 5 maanga — wo memory me nahi hai, disk (swap) pe hai
    • → PAGE FAULT! CPU ruk gaya, OS disk se page laaya
    • → Page ko khaali frame me daala, page table update ki
    • → Program dobara chala — ab page mil gaya ✓
    • → Zyada page faults hone lage to system slow ho jata hai (thrashing)

5. Paged segmentation — dono ka combination

StepKya hota hai
1. Segment karoProgram ko logical segments me baanto (code/data/stack)
2. Page karoHar segment ko fixed-size pages me kaato
3. Translate karoSegment table → page table → physical frame
FaydaLogical structure + no external fragmentation

Modern OS (Linux, Windows) yahi karte hain — segmentation ka logical fayda, paging ka physical fayda, dono saath.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Paging aur segmentation ko ek hi samajhna: Paging fixed-size physical division hai, segmentation variable-size logical division — dono ka purpose alag hai.
  2. Internal aur external fragmentation ko ulta samajhna: Internal = page ke andar waste (paging). External = beech me gaps (segmentation).
  3. Segfault ko random crash samajhna: Segfault ka matlab hai tumne apne segment ki limit se bahar access kiya — aksar galat pointer ya buffer overflow ki nishani hai.
  4. Page table ko free samajhna: Badi page tables khud memory khati hain — isliye multi-level page tables aur TLB use hote hain.
  5. Virtual memory ko RAM samajhna: Virtual memory ek illusion hai — har process ko lagta hai uske paas poori memory hai, asli me pages disk aur RAM ke beech aate-jaate rehte hain.

7. Interview corner

Q: Paging aur segmentation me farq kya hai?

Paging memory ko fixed-size pages (4KB) me baant ta hai — physical division, external fragmentation nahi hoti. Segmentation program ko logical parts (code/data/stack) me baant ta hai — har segment ka size alag hota hai, external fragmentation hoti hai, par protection aur sharing aasan hai.

Q: Internal aur external fragmentation me farq?

Internal fragmentation paging me hoti hai — aakhri page aadha khaali reh jata hai (page ke andar waste). External fragmentation segmentation me hoti hai — memory me chhote gaps ban jate hain jinme koi segment fit nahi hota, halanki total jagah kaafi hai.

Q: Page fault kya hota hai?

Jab CPU kisi page ko access karta hai jo physical memory me nahi hai (disk/swap pe hai) to page fault hota hai — OS page ko disk se laake memory me daalta hai, page table update karta hai, aur program dobara chalata hai. Zyada page faults se thrashing hoti hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Paging me memory ko kis size me baanta jata hai?

  • Alag-alag size ke segments me
  • Fixed-size pages me (jaise 4KB) ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Ek hi bada block me
  • Files me

Sawaal 2: Segmentation fault (segfault) kab aata hai?

  • Jab page disk pe ho
  • Jab program apne segment ki limit se bahar access kare ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Jab RAM full ho
  • Jab CPU garam ho
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Paging = fixed-size pages, no external fragmentation, internal waste; Segmentation = logical segments, protection/sharing aasan, external fragmentation; modern OS dono ko milake (paged segmentation) use karte hain.
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-are-the-differences-between-paging-and-segmentation.md
Agla02 · IPv4 vs. IPv6: Differences
02Computer Fundamentals · Guide 02 / 12

IPv4 vs. IPv6: Differences

Internet ke har device ka ek address hota hai — IP address. IPv4 (jaise 192.168.1.1) 1980s se chal raha hai, par uske addresses khatam ho gaye. IPv6 (jaise 2001:db8::1) iska replacement hai — itne addresses ki har ret ke dane ko bhi ek mil jaye. Par transition itna slow kyun hai?

1. IPv4 vs IPv6 — phone number wali kahani

IPv4: Socho ek sheher me phone numbers sirf 4-digit ke hain — 0000 se 9999, matlab sirf 10,000 numbers. Sheher badh gaya, log zyada ho gaye — numbers khatam! Log ek hi number share karne lage (NAT — ek number ke peeche kai log).

IPv6: Ab numbers 10-digit ke kar diye — itne numbers ki har aadmi ko 100 numbers mil sakte hain. Kisi ko share karne ki zaroorat nahi, har device ka apna unique number.

Numbers: IPv4 = 32-bit → 4.3 billion addresses. IPv6 = 128-bit → 340 undecillion (3.4 × 1038) addresses. Har device ko unique address, NAT ki zaroorat nahi.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

IPv4 — purana, par har jagah

Format: 4 numbers, dot se jude — 192.168.1.1. Har number 0-255 (8-bit). Total 232 = 4.3 billion addresses — jo 2011 me hi khatam ho gaye (IANA ne aakhri block de diya).

Bachao ka tareeka — NAT: Ghar/office ke saare devices ek public IP share karte hain — router private IPs (192.168.x.x) ko ek public IP me badal deta hai. Isse IPv4 zinda raha, par peer-to-peer connection mushkil ho gaya.

Header: 20 bytes, variable — options aur checksum hote hain, jo router ko slow karte hain.

IPv6 — naya, bada, fast

Format: 8 groups, colon se jude, hexadecimal — 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334 (chhota likho to 2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334). Har group 16-bit.

Address types: Unicast (ek ko), Multicast (group ko), Anycast (sabse paas wale ko). Broadcast nahi hai — multicast use hota hai.

Header: 40 bytes, fixed — simple hai, router fast process karta hai. Checksum nahi hai (lower layers pe chhod diya). IPsec built-in hai — encryption/authentication ka support header me hi hai.

Auto-configuration (SLAAC): Device khud apna address bana sakta hai — DHCP ki zaroorat nahi. Plug karo, address mil gaya.

Transition — dono saath kaise chalte hain?

IPv4 se IPv6 me ek din me switch nahi ho sakta — duniya bhar ke routers, devices, software badalne honge. Isliye transition mechanisms hain:

Dual-stack: Device dono protocols chalata hai — jahan IPv6 mile, wahan IPv6, warna IPv4. Aaj ka sabse common tareeka.

Tunneling: IPv6 packets ko IPv4 ke andar lapet ke bhejo (6to4, Teredo) — IPv4 network ke upar IPv6 chalao.

Translation (NAT64): IPv6-only device ko IPv4 site se jodne ke liye translator beech me.

Google ke stats: duniya ka ~45% traffic IPv6 pe hai (2024) — India me 70%+! Mobile networks (Jio) ne IPv6 adoption ko badhaya hai.

IPv6 ke fayde — sirf addresses nahi

1) No NAT: Har device ka unique public address — peer-to-peer, gaming, IoT aasan. 2) Better routing: Simple header, fast routers. 3) Built-in security: IPsec mandatory support. 4) Auto-config: SLAAC se device khud address banata hai. 5) IoT ready: Arabon devices — har sensor, har bulb ka apna address.

Challenges: Logon ko hexadecimal address yaad rakhna mushkil (isliye DNS zaroori hai), purane devices/software IPv6 support nahi karte, aur security teams ko naye protocol ki training chahiye.

3. Side-by-side comparison

CheezIPv4IPv6
Address size32-bit128-bit
Total addresses4.3 billion340 undecillion
Format192.168.1.1 (decimal)2001:db8::1 (hex)
Header20 bytes, variable40 bytes, fixed
ChecksumHaanNahi
NATZaroori (addresses kam)Zaroorat nahi
BroadcastHaanNahi (multicast)
IPsecOptionalBuilt-in
Auto-configDHCP chahiyeSLAAC (khud bana lo)

4. Try karo — address banao aur compare karo

IPv4 aur IPv6 addresses banao, unhe chhota likho, aur dekho NAT ke bina kaise har device ko unique address milta hai.

  1. 1. IPv4 address dekho
    • → Tumhara ghar ka public IP: 103.21.45.67
    • → Ghar ke andar: 5 devices — phone, laptop, TV, fridge, bulb
    • → Sab ek hi public IP share karte hain (NAT ke through)
    • → Private IPs: 192.168.1.2, 192.168.1.3, ...
    • → Bahar se koi seedha tumhare bulb se connect nahi kar sakta — NAT beech me hai
  2. 2. IPv4 khatam — kitne bache?
    • → Total IPv4: 4,294,967,296 (4.3 billion)
    • → Duniya ke devices: 15+ billion — addresses se 3x zyada!
    • → IANA ne 2011 me aakhri block de diya — ab naye addresses nahi bante
    • → Isi liye NAT aur CGNAT use hota hai — sharing hi ek raasta bacha tha
  3. 3. IPv6 address banao
    • → Tumhara IPv6: 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334
    • → Chhota likho: 2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334 (zero groups ko :: se badlo)
    • → Total: 340,282,366,920,938,463,463,374,607,431,768,211,456 addresses!
    • → Har device ko unique public address — phone, laptop, TV, bulb, sabko alag
    • → NAT ki zaroorat hi nahi — har device seedha internet pe hai
  4. 4. Dual-stack try karo
    • → Tumhara laptop dual-stack hai: IPv4 + IPv6 dono on hain
    • → google.com kholo: DNS ne IPv6 address diya → IPv6 se connect hua ✓
    • → Purani site kholo (sirf IPv4): IPv4 se connect hua ✓
    • → Browser khud chun leta hai — tumhe kuch karna nahi padta
    • → India me Jio pe IPv6 adoption 70%+ hai — tum shayad abhi IPv6 hi use kar rahe ho!

5. IPv6 address ke types

TypeMatlabExample
UnicastEk device ko2001:db8::1
MulticastEk group koff02::1 (saare nodes)
AnycastSabse paas wale koDNS servers (ek IP, kai servers)
Link-localEk hi network mefe80::/10
LoopbackKhud ko::1 (= 127.0.0.1)

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. IPv6 ko 'sirf zyada addresses' samajhna: Iske saath simpler header, built-in IPsec, auto-config aur no-NAT bhi aate hain — ye poora upgrade hai.
  2. IPv6 address ko yaad karne ki koshish: Hexadecimal addresses yaad nahi hote — DNS use karo, jaise IPv4 me bhi karte ho.
  3. IPv6 on karke firewall bhoolna: NAT ek accidental firewall tha — IPv6 me har device public hai, to host firewall zaroori hai.
  4. Transition ko 'ek din ka kaam' samajhna: Dual-stack saalon tak chalega — dono protocols ko secure karna padta hai, sirf ek ko nahi.
  5. IPv4 private ranges ko IPv6 me dhoondhna: IPv6 me NAT nahi hai — private addressing ka concept alag hai (ULA fc00::/7).

7. Interview corner

Q: IPv4 ke addresses kyun khatam ho gaye?

IPv4 32-bit hai — sirf 4.3 billion addresses. Devices 15 billion se zyada ho gaye. NAT ne time diya, par permanent solution IPv6 hai — 128-bit, 340 undecillion addresses.

Q: IPv6 IPv4 se behtar kaise hai?

Zyada addresses ke alawa: simpler fixed header (fast routing), built-in IPsec, auto-configuration (SLAAC), no NAT (har device unique), aur multicast se broadcast ki jagah — network efficient hota hai.

Q: Dual-stack kya hai?

Device dono protocols (IPv4 + IPv6) ek saath chalata hai. Jahan IPv6 available ho, wahan IPv6 use hota hai, warna IPv4. Ye IPv4 se IPv6 transition ka sabse common tareeka hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: IPv4 me kitne addresses hote hain?

  • 340 undecillion
  • 4.3 billion (32-bit) ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Infinite
  • 1 million

Sawaal 2: IPv6 me NAT ki zaroorat kyun nahi hai?

  • IPv6 fast hai
  • Addresses itne zyada hain ki har device ko unique public address mil sakta hai ✓ Sahi jawab
  • IPv6 me security nahi hoti
  • IPv6 me DNS nahi hota
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: IPv4 = 32-bit, 4.3B addresses, khatam ho gaye, NAT se zinda hai; IPv6 = 128-bit, 340 undecillion, no NAT, built-in IPsec, SLAAC auto-config; transition dual-stack se ho raha hai.
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/ipv4-vs-ipv6.md
Pichla01 · Paging vs SegmentationAgla03 · Top 4 Most Popular Use Cases for UDP
03Computer Fundamentals · Guide 03 / 12

Top 4 Most Popular Use Cases for UDP

TCP har jagah hai — par kuch kaam aise hain jahan TCP slow padta hai. Wahan UDP aata hai: no connection, no guarantee, par lightning fast. Is page me UDP ke 4 sabse popular use cases samjho — aur kyun inme 'data kho jaye to chalega, par delay nahi chalega'.

1. UDP vs TCP — postcard vs registered post

TCP registered post hai: letter milega hi milega, order me milega, aur mile to confirmation milega — par slow hai, aur har letter ke liye pehle phone karke connection banana padta hai.

UDP postcard hai: likho, phek do — pahuncha to pahuncha, nahi to nahi. Koi confirmation nahi, koi order nahi. Par bahut fast hai — aur ek saath hazaaron postcards bhej sakte ho.

UDP ka rule: 'Speed > Reliability'. Jahan ek packet kho jaye to koi farq nahi padta (agle packet me naya data aa jayega), wahan UDP jeetta hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

1. Live Streaming aur Video Calls

Video call me har frame (image) ek packet hai. Ek frame kho jaye to kya hoga? Screen pe ek chhota sa glitch — agle frame me sab theek. Par agar TCP use karo to khoya frame dobara aayega — aur tab tak video ruk jayega (buffering). Call me 2 second ki delay se baat-cheet kharab ho jati hai.

Isliye Zoom, Google Meet, YouTube Live — sab UDP (ya UDP-based QUIC) use karte hain. Thoda data kho jaye to chalega, par real-time hona chahiye.

Example: 30 fps video me ek frame kho gaya — tumhe pata bhi nahi chalega. TCP me wo frame dobara aane tak video freeze ho jata.

2. Online Gaming

Game me har millisecond matter karta hai. Tumhara character aage badha — ye info server ko turant chahiye. Ek packet kho jaye to agle packet me nayi position aa jayegi — purani position ka koi matlab nahi.

TCP me khoya packet dobara aayega — aur tab tak game ruk jayega (lag). UDP me game chalta rehta hai — thoda glitch, par khel rukta nahi.

Reliable UDP: Kai games UDP ke upar apna khud ka reliability layer banate hain — zaroori packets (jaise 'player ne shoot kiya') ko dobara bhejte hain, baaki ko nahi. Best of both worlds.

3. DNS Lookups

Har website kholne se pehle DNS query hoti hai: 'google.com ka IP kya hai?' Ye query chhoti hoti hai (ek packet me aa jati hai), aur jawab bhi chhota hota hai.

TCP use karo to pehle connection banana padega (3-way handshake) — ek chhoti query ke liye itna overhead? UDP me ek packet bhejo, ek packet me jawab aa gaya — fast.

Agar jawab na aaye to client dobara bhej deta hai (timeout pe retry). DNS ke liye UDP default hai; bade responses (DNSSEC) ke liye TCP use hota hai.

4. IoT aur Broadcasting

IoT sensors: Temperature sensor har second ek chhota packet bhejta hai. Ek packet kho jaye to agle second naya aayega — purane ka koi matlab nahi. TCP ka overhead (connection, ACK) chhote device ki battery kha jayega.

Broadcasting/Multicast: Ek packet, kai log — live TV, stock market data. TCP me har receiver se alag connection banana padega — UDP multicast me ek packet sabko jata hai.

DHCP, SNMP, NTP (time sync): Ye sab chhote, fast protocols UDP pe chalte hain — inme reliability se zyada speed matter karti hai.

3. UDP vs TCP — kab kya?

CheezTCPUDP
ConnectionHaan (3-way handshake)Nahi
ReliabilityGuaranteed, order meKoi guarantee nahi
SpeedSlow (overhead)Fast
UseWeb, email, file transferVideo, gaming, DNS, IoT
Header20 bytes8 bytes

QUIC: Google ka protocol — UDP ke upar TCP jaisi reliability banata hai. HTTP/3 QUIC pe chalta hai — web bhi fast, reliable bhi. UDP ka future yahi hai.

4. Try karo — video call TCP vs UDP

Ek video call chal rahi hai. Pehle TCP se, phir UDP se — dekho ek packet kho jaye to kya hota hai.

  1. 1. Video call — TCP se
    • → Frame 1, 2, 3 bheje gaye... Frame 4 KHO GAYA (network me)
    • → TCP: 'Frame 4 nahi mila — dobara bhejo!'
    • → Sender ne Frame 4 dobara bheja — tab tak Frame 5, 6 ruk gaye
    • → Video FREEZE ho gaya 2 second ke liye — phir chala
    • → Baat-cheet me delay — 'Hello... hello? Tum ruk gaye the!'
    • ✗ TCP video call me LAG deta hai
  2. 2. Video call — UDP se
    • → Frame 1, 2, 3 bheje gaye... Frame 4 KHO GAYA
    • → UDP: koi dobara nahi bhejta — Frame 5 aa gaya
    • → Screen pe ek chhota sa glitch (1 frame) — tumhe pata bhi nahi chala
    • → Call chalti rahi, bina ruke, bina delay ke ✓
    • ✓ UDP real-time ke liye BEST hai
  3. 3. DNS query — UDP se
    • → Query: google.com ka IP kya hai?
    • → UDP packet bheja — 20ms me jawab aaya: 142.250.80.46 ✓
    • → TCP hota to pehle handshake (60ms) phir query — 3x slow!
    • → Jawab na aaye to client dobara bhej deta hai (retry)
  4. 4. Game — UDP se
    • → Tumne shoot kiya — packet bheja, par kho gaya
    • → Game ne zaroori packet ko dobara bheja (reliable UDP layer)
    • → Position updates (har frame) — kho jaye to chalega, agla aa jayega
    • → Result: game smooth chala, lag nahi hua ✓
    • → TCP hota to har khoya packet game ko rok deta

5. UDP ke 4 use cases — ek table me

#Use CaseKyun UDP?Example
1Live streaming / video callsReal-time chahiye, frame kho jaye to chalegaZoom, YouTube Live
2Online gamingLow latency, purani position bekaarPUBG, Valorant
3DNS lookupsChhoti query, fast jawab chahiyeHar website kholne se pehle
4IoT / broadcast / multicastChhote packets, kai receivers, batterySensors, live TV, NTP

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Har cheez ke liye UDP use karna: File download ya payment me data kho jaye to tabahi hai — wahan TCP chahiye.
  2. UDP ko 'unreliable' keh ke bekaar samajhna: UDP ke upar reliability banayi ja sakti hai (QUIC, reliable UDP) — zaroori packets dobara bhejo, baaki ko jaane do.
  3. UDP me order assume karna: Packets kisi bhi order me aa sakte hain — application ko order handle karna padta hai (sequence numbers).
  4. UDP ko firewall me block kar dena: Kai firewalls UDP block karte hain — video calls aur gaming fail ho jati hain. Zaroori UDP ports kholo.
  5. TCP aur UDP ke ports ko ek samajhna: Port 53 TCP aur port 53 UDP alag hain — DNS dono pe chalta hai, alag kaam ke liye.

7. Interview corner

Q: UDP ke 4 main use cases kaunse hain?

Live streaming/video calls, online gaming, DNS lookups, aur IoT/broadcasting. In sab me speed aur real-time delivery reliability se zyada important hai — ek packet kho jaye to agla packet uski jagah le leta hai.

Q: Video calls me TCP kyun nahi use karte?

Kyunki TCP khoya packet dobara bhejta hai — aur tab tak video ruk jata hai (buffering/lag). Real-time call me delay se baat-cheet kharab ho jati hai. UDP me khoya frame skip ho jata hai, call chalti rehti hai.

Q: DNS UDP kyun use karta hai?

Kyunki DNS query chhoti hoti hai aur jawab fast chahiye. TCP me pehle 3-way handshake karna padega — ek chhoti query ke liye bahut overhead hai. UDP me ek packet me query, ek me jawab. Bade responses ke liye TCP use hota hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Video call ke liye UDP TCP se behtar kyun hai?

  • UDP me data kabhi nahi khota
  • UDP fast hai — khoya frame skip ho jata hai, call rukti nahi ✓ Sahi jawab
  • UDP free hai
  • UDP me video quality zyada hoti hai

Sawaal 2: DNS lookup ke liye UDP kyun use hota hai?

  • DNS ko reliability nahi chahiye
  • Query chhoti hai — TCP handshake ka overhead bekaar hai ✓ Sahi jawab
  • DNS sirf UDP pe chalta hai
  • TCP DNS support nahi karta
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: UDP = fast, no connection, no guarantee; use karo jahan speed > reliability: video calls, gaming, DNS, IoT; file/payment jaisi cheezon ke liye TCP; QUIC UDP ke upar reliability banata hai.
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/top-4-most-popular-use-cases-for-udp.md
Pichla02 · IPv4 vs. IPv6: DifferencesAgla04 · How Does the Domain Name System (DNS) Lookup Work?
04Computer Fundamentals · Guide 04 / 12

How Does the Domain Name System (DNS) Lookup Work?

Tum google.com type karte ho aur site khul jati hai — par computer ko google.com se koi matlab nahi, use IP address chahiye. DNS wahi phonebook hai jo naam ko IP me badalta hai. Is page me poora lookup — browser se leke root server tak — samjho.

1. DNS — phonebook wali kahani

Socho tumhe apne dost Priya ko phone karna hai. Tumhe uska naam pata hai, par phone karne ke liye number chahiye. Tum phonebook kholte ho, 'Priya' dhoondhte ho, number milta hai, phir phone karte ho.

DNS wahi phonebook hai: tum google.com (naam) dete ho, DNS 142.250.80.46 (number/IP) deta hai, phir browser us IP se connect karta hai. Bina DNS ke tumhe har site ka IP yaad rakhna padta — 142.250.80.46 yaad hai? Nahi na.

Ek line me: DNS = internet ki phonebook. Naam → IP address. Har website kholne se pehle ek DNS lookup hota hai.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Step 1 — Browser aur OS cache

Pehle browser apna cache dekhta hai: 'Kya maine google.com ko pehle khola tha? IP yaad hai?' Haan to turant connect — koi lookup nahi.

Nahi to OS (system) apna cache dekhta hai, phir /etc/hosts file dekhta hai (jisme manual entries hoti hain — developers yahan test domains daalte hain).

Cache me TTL (Time To Live) hota hai — IP kitne time tak valid hai. TTL khatam hua to dobara lookup karna padega. Isliye pehli visit slow, doosri fast hoti hai.

Step 2 — Recursive Resolver (ISP ka DNS)

Cache me nahi mila to request recursive resolver ko jati hai — aam taur pe tumhare ISP ka DNS server (ya 8.8.8.8 Google DNS, 1.1.1.1 Cloudflare). Resolver tumhare liye poora lookup karta hai — tumhe sirf jawab milta hai.

Resolver bhi pehle apna cache dekhta hai — lakhon log google.com kholte hain, to jawab aksar cache me hi mil jata hai. Isliye aam sites ka lookup fast hota hai.

Step 3 — Root, TLD, Authoritative servers

Cache me nahi mila to resolver root server se poochta hai: '.com kahan hai?' Root kehta hai: 'TLD server pe jao' (13 root servers duniya bhar me hain, par anycast se kai copies hain).

TLD server (.com): 'google.com kaun handle karta hai? Authoritative server pe jao.' Authoritative server: Google ka apna DNS server — 'google.com = 142.250.80.46'. Ye final jawab hai.

Resolver jawab ko cache karta hai (TTL tak) aur tumhe deta hai. Ab browser IP se connect karta hai — website khul gayi!

DNS Record Types — kya-kya pooch sakte ho?

A: Domain → IPv4 address. AAAA: Domain → IPv6 address. CNAME: Ek domain ka alias — www.google.com → google.com. MX: Mail server — email kahan jaye. TXT: Text — verification, SPF/DKIM (email security). NS: Kaunsa server authoritative hai.

Example: Tum mail.google.com kholo to A record se IP milta hai; email bhejo to MX record se mail server milta hai.

DNS over HTTPS (DoH): DNS queries bhi encrypt hoti hain — ISP ko nahi pata tum kaunsi sites khol rahe ho.

3. Poora DNS lookup — ek saath

Tum: google.com type kiya
1. Browser cache? → nahi mila
2. OS cache / /etc/hosts? → nahi mila
3. Resolver (8.8.8.8) ko query → uske cache me? → nahi mila
4. Resolver → Root server: ".com kahan hai?"
   Root: "TLD (.com) server: 192.33.4.12"
5. Resolver → TLD server: "google.com kahan hai?"
   TLD: "Authoritative server: ns1.google.com"
6. Resolver → Authoritative: "google.com ka IP?"
   Auth: "142.250.80.46"
7. Resolver → Tum: "142.250.80.46" (cache me save, TTL tak)
8. Browser → 142.250.80.46:443 connect → website khul gayi!

# Total time: pehli baar ~50-100ms, cache se ~1ms

4. Try karo — DNS lookup karo

google.com kholo aur har step dekho. Phir ek nayi site aur ek galat site bhi try karo — kya hota hai?

  1. 1. google.com kholo (pehli baar)
    • → Browser cache: khaali ✗
    • → OS cache: khaali ✗
    • → Resolver (8.8.8.8): cache me mila! (lakhon log kholte hain)
    • → Jawab: 142.250.80.46 — 20ms me
    • → Browser connect hua → Google khul gaya ✓
    • → Resolver ne jawab cache kar liya (TTL: 300 sec)
  2. 2. Ek nayi site kholo (cache me nahi)
    • → Site: mynewsite123.com — kisi ke cache me nahi hai
    • → Resolver → Root: '.com kahan hai?'
    • → Root → TLD (.com): 'Authoritative server ka pata diya'
    • → TLD → Authoritative: 'IP hai 93.184.216.34'
    • → Resolver → Tum: IP mil gaya — 80ms lage
    • → Browser connect hua ✓ — agli baar cache se fast milega
  3. 3. Dobara wahi site kholo (cache hit)
    • → Browser cache: mil gaya! IP yaad hai (TTL abhi valid hai)
    • → Koi DNS lookup hi nahi hua — turant connect ✓
    • → Isi liye doosri visit pehli se fast hoti hai
  4. 4. Galat domain type karo
    • → Tumne likha: gogle.con (galat spelling)
    • → Resolver → Root → TLD: '.con TLD hi nahi hai!'
    • → Jawab: NXDOMAIN (domain exist hi nahi karta)
    • → Browser: 'Site nahi mili' — ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED
    • → Check karo: spelling theek hai?
  5. 5. DNS hijack (attack) dekho
    • → Attacker ne tumhare DNS ko badal diya — google.com ka IP uske server ka hai!
    • → Tum google.com kholte ho — fake site khulti hai ✗
    • → Bachao: DNSSEC (signed answers) + DNS over HTTPS (DoH)
    • → DoH on hai to ISP/attacker DNS queries nahi padh sakta ✓

5. DNS servers — kaun kya karta hai?

ServerKaam
Recursive ResolverTumhare liye poora lookup karta hai (ISP/Google DNS)
Root ServerTLD servers ka pata deta hai (13 logical, anycast copies)
TLD Server.com/.in/.org ke authoritative servers ka pata deta hai
Authoritative ServerFinal jawab — domain ka asli IP deta hai

Public DNS: Google 8.8.8.8, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 — ISP ke DNS se fast aur private hote hain.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. DNS ko slow samajh ke ignore karna: DNS lookup har visit pe hota hai — slow DNS matlab slow website. Fast resolver (1.1.1.1) use karo.
  2. TTL ko bahut lamba rakhna: Server ka IP badla, par purana IP cache me 1 din tak raha — users purane server pe jaate rahe. Migration se pehle TTL kam karo.
  3. DNSSEC na lagana: Bina DNSSEC ke DNS answers ko fake kiya ja sakta hai (DNS spoofing). Important domains pe DNSSEC lagao.
  4. Single DNS provider pe bharosa: DNS provider down hua to site gayab — secondary DNS provider rakho.
  5. /etc/hosts ko bhoolna: Local testing me hosts file se domain ko localhost pe point karo — DNS ka intezaar mat karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: DNS lookup kaise kaam karta hai?

Browser pehle apna cache, phir OS cache dekhta hai. Nahi mila to recursive resolver (ISP/Google DNS) se poochta hai. Resolver root server se TLD server ka pata, TLD se authoritative server ka pata, aur authoritative se final IP leta hai. Jawab cache hota hai, phir browser IP se connect karta hai.

Q: Recursive aur authoritative DNS me farq?

Recursive resolver tumhare liye poora lookup karta hai — root se leke authoritative tak jaake jawab lata hai. Authoritative server ek domain ka final source hota hai — uske paas domain ke records hote hain, wo kisi aur se nahi poochta.

Q: DNS caching kyun zaroori hai?

Kyunki har lookup me root → TLD → authoritative tak jaana slow hota hai (50-100ms). Cache (browser, OS, resolver) se jawab 1ms me milta hai. TTL batata hai cache kitne time tak valid hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: DNS ka main kaam kya hai?

  • Website banana
  • Domain naam ko IP address me badalna ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Password store karna
  • Email bhejna

Sawaal 2: DNS lookup me sabse pehle kya check hota hai?

  • Root server
  • Browser aur OS ka cache ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Authoritative server
  • TLD server
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: DNS = internet ki phonebook (naam → IP); lookup: browser cache → OS cache → resolver → root → TLD → authoritative; cache aur TTL se fast hota hai; DNSSEC aur DoH se secure hota hai.
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-does-the-domain-name-system-dns-lookup-work.md
Pichla03 · Top 4 Most Popular Use Cases for UDPAgla05 · DNS Record Types You Should Know
05Computer Fundamentals · Guide 05 / 12

DNS Record Types You Should Know

DNS sirf naam ko IP me nahi badalta — uske alag-alag record types hain, har ek ek alag kaam ke liye: website khulwana, email pahunchana, domain verify karwana, security lagana. Is page me wo record types samjho jo har developer ko aane chahiye.

1. DNS records — phonebook ke alag-alag columns

Socho ek phonebook hai jisme har naam ke saamne kai columns hain: phone number (A record), ghar ka address (AAAA), nickname (CNAME — Canonical Name — 'Priya' ko 'Pihu' bhi kehte hain), postman ka address (MX — chitthi kahan jaye), aur notes (TXT — 'ye number verified hai').

Har column ka apna kaam hai — tumhe jis cheez ki zaroorat hai, tum wahi column dekhte ho. Website kholni hai to A record, email bhejni hai to MX record, domain verify karna hai to TXT record.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

A aur AAAA — website ka address

A record: Domain → IPv4 address. google.com → 142.250.80.46. Ye sabse common record hai — website kholne ke liye yahi chahiye.

AAAA record: Domain → IPv6 address. google.com → 2607:f8b0:4004:800::200e. IPv6 ke liye chahiye — aaj kal dono rakhte hain (dual-stack).

Example: Tum example.com kholte ho — browser A record se IP nikalta hai, phir connect karta hai. A record na ho to site khulegi hi nahi.

CNAME — nickname / alias

CNAME: Ek domain ko doosre domain ka alias banao. www.example.com → example.com — matlab www wala bhi wahi site khole.

Use: Subdomains ko ek jagah point karna — blog.example.com → example.hashnode.com. IP badla to sirf ek jagah badlo, saare CNAME apne aap follow karenge.

Rule: CNAME wale naam pe aur koi record nahi ho sakta (A, MX — kuch nahi). Aur root domain (example.com) pe CNAME nahi lagta — isliye www pe CNAME, root pe A record lagate hain.

MX — email kahan jaye?

MX record: Is domain ke emails kaunsa mail server lega? example.com → mail.example.com (priority 10). Priority kam = pehle try karo.

Example: Tum priya@example.com ko email bhejte ho — tumhara mail server example.com ka MX record dhoondhta hai, phir us server ko email bhejta hai.

MX na ho to email deliver hi nahi hogi — 'address not found' aayega. Gmail/Google Workspace use karte ho to unke MX records lagane padte hain.

TXT, NS, SOA — verification aur control

TXT: Free text — domain verify karne ke liye (Google Search Console: 'google-site-verification=...'), email security ke liye (SPF, DKIM, DMARC records — ye batate hain kaunsi server tumhare naam se email bhej sakti hai).

NS: Kaunsa server is domain ka authoritative hai — example.com → ns1.cloudflare.com. Domain kharida to registrar pe NS records batate hain DNS kahan manage hoga.

SOA: Zone ki jaankari — primary server, admin email, refresh time. Har zone me ek SOA hota hai.

PTR: Ulta — IP → domain (reverse DNS). Email servers spam check ke liye dekhte hain.

3. Records — ek table me

RecordKaamExample
ADomain → IPv4example.com → 93.184.216.34
AAAADomain → IPv6example.com → 2606:2800:220:1::248
CNAMEDomain ka aliaswww → example.com
MXMail serverexample.com → mail.example.com (10)
TXTText / verificationgoogle-site-verification=abc123
NSAuthoritative serverexample.com → ns1.cloudflare.com
SOAZone infoPrimary server + admin
PTRIP → Domain (reverse)93.184.216.34 → example.com
SRVService location_sip._tcp → sipserver:5060
CAAKaun CA certificate de sakta hai0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
# Terminal se records dekho:
dig example.com A        # A record
dig example.com MX       # mail server
dig example.com TXT      # verification records
nslookup example.com     # simple lookup (Windows/Linux)

4. Try karo — ek domain setup karo

Tumne example.com kharida hai. Website, email aur verification — har ek ke liye sahi DNS record lagao.

  1. 1. Website chalao — A record
    • → Server ka IP: 93.184.216.34
    • → A record lagaya: example.com → 93.184.216.34
    • → AAAA bhi lagaya (IPv6): → 2606:2800:220:1::248
    • → Browser me example.com kholo — website khul gayi ✓
    • → www ke liye CNAME: www.example.com → example.com ✓
  2. 2. Email chalao — MX record
    • → Gmail (Google Workspace) use karna hai
    • → MX records lagaye: ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM (priority 1), ALT1... (5), ALT2... (5)
    • → Test email bheji: priya@example.com → Google ke server pe pahunchi ✓
    • → MX na lagate to email kabhi deliver nahi hoti ✗
  3. 3. Domain verify karo — TXT record
    • → Google Search Console: 'Apna domain verify karo'
    • → TXT record lagaya: google-site-verification=abc123xyz
    • → Google ne TXT padha → domain tumhara hai, verify ho gaya ✓
    • → SPF record bhi lagaya: 'v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all'
    • → Ab tumhare naam se sirf Google ke servers email bhej sakte hain — spam/phishing se bachao ✓
  4. 4. Galat record — kya hota hai?
    • → Tumne galti se A record me galat IP daal diya: 1.2.3.4
    • → Website kholo to galat server khulta hai (ya kuch nahi)
    • → TTL 1 ghanta hai — fix karne ke baad bhi 1 ghanta purana IP cache me rahega
    • → Lesson: bade badlav se pehle TTL kam karo (5 min) — phir badlo, phir TTL wapas badhao

5. Email security records — SPF, DKIM, DMARC

RecordKaam
SPF (TXT)Kaunsi servers tumhare naam se email bhej sakti hain
DKIM (TXT)Email ko sign karo — receiver verify kare ki email badli nahi
DMARC (TXT)SPF/DKIM fail ho to kya karo — reject ya quarantine

Teeno mil ke email spoofing rokte hain — bina inke tumhare naam se koi bhi fake email bhej sakta hai.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Root domain pe CNAME lagana: CNAME wale naam pe aur koi record nahi ho sakta — root pe A record lagao, www pe CNAME.
  2. MX record bhoolna: Website chal gayi, email nahi — kyunki MX lagana bhool gaye. Domain setup me email mat bhoolo.
  3. TTL ko hamesha bada rakhna: Migration ya IP change se pehle TTL kam karo — warna purana record ghanton tak cache me rahega.
  4. SPF/DKIM/DMARC na lagana: Bina inke tumhare domain se spoofed email bhej ke phishing ho sakti hai — aur tumhari emails spam me jayengi.
  5. DNS changes ko test na karna: Badlav ke baad dig se check karo — galat record ghanton tak users ko affect karega.

7. Interview corner

Q: A, CNAME aur MX records me farq?

A record domain ko IPv4 address se jodta hai (website ke liye). CNAME ek domain ko doosre domain ka alias banata hai. MX record batata hai is domain ke emails kaunsa mail server lega.

Q: TXT record kis kaam aata hai?

TXT me free text hota hai — domain verification (Google Search Console), aur email security (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) ke liye. Ye batata hai kaunsi servers tumhare naam se email bhej sakti hain aur email asli hai ya nahi.

Q: CNAME root domain pe kyun nahi lagta?

Kyunki CNAME wale naam pe aur koi record nahi ho sakta — par root domain pe NS aur SOA records hone zaroori hain. Isliye root pe A/AAAA record, aur www jaise subdomains pe CNAME lagate hain.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Website kholne ke liye kaunsa DNS record chahiye?

  • MX
  • A (ya AAAA) ✓ Sahi jawab
  • TXT
  • PTR

Sawaal 2: Email kis record se pata chalta hai ki kahan jaye?

  • A record
  • MX record ✓ Sahi jawab
  • CNAME
  • NS record
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: A/AAAA = website ka IP; CNAME = alias; MX = mail server; TXT = verification + SPF/DKIM/DMARC; NS = authoritative server; har record ka apna kaam hai — galat record matlab site ya email band.
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/dns-record-types-you-should-know.md
Pichla04 · How Does the Domain Name System (DNS) Lookup Work?Agla06 · TCP vs UDP for Online Gaming
06Computer Fundamentals · Guide 06 / 12

TCP vs UDP for Online Gaming

Game me ek second ki delay matlab haar. Online gaming kaunsa protocol use karta hai — TCP ya UDP? Jawab hai: UDP, par uske upar ek khud ka reliability layer. Is page me samjho kyun, aur kaise games 'reliable UDP' banate hain.

1. Gaming — walkie-talkie vs phone call

TCP phone call hai: 'Hello? Sun rahe ho? Maine kaha — aage badho. Dobara kaho, samajh nahi aaya.' Har baat ki confirmation, har baat order me — par slow.

UDP walkie-talkie hai: 'Aage badho — over!' Bolo aur aage badho. Koi confirmation nahi, koi dobara nahi. Agar ek baat nahi suni to agli baat me nayi info aa jayegi — 'Ab left jao — over!'

Game me walkie-talkie jeetta hai — kyunki 100ms purani position ka koi matlab nahi, nayi position chahiye. Par 'maine shoot kiya' jaisi baat kho jaye to nuksaan hai — isliye games zaroori baaton ke liye walkie-talkie pe bhi 'confirm karo' bolte hain.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Kyun UDP? — latency hi sab kuch hai

Game me latency (ping) sab kuch hai. 20ms ping wala player 100ms wale se hamesha jeettega — kyunki uski goli pehle chalegi.

TCP me har packet ka ACK chahiye, khoya packet dobara aata hai (retransmission), aur packets order me aate hain (head-of-line blocking — ek packet atka to saare ruk gaye). Ye sab delay badhata hai — game ke liye zeher hai.

UDP me koi handshake nahi, koi ACK nahi, koi order nahi — packet bhejo, bhool jao. Latency minimum. Ek packet kho jaye to agle packet me nayi position aa jayegi.

Reliable UDP — dono ka best

Games seedha UDP nahi use karte — wo UDP ke upar apna reliability layer banate hain:

Zaroori packets (reliable): 'Player ne shoot kiya', 'Player mar gaya', 'Score badla' — ye kho jaye to game galat ho jayega. Inhe sequence number deke, ACK maang ke, dobara bhej ke guarantee karte hain.

Non-zaroori packets (unreliable): 'Player ki position (x=10, y=20)' — har frame naya packet aata hai, purana bekaar. Inhe dobara nahi bhejte.

Example: Valve (CS:GO), Riot (Valorant), Epic (Fortnite) — sab UDP + custom reliability use karte hain. QUIC bhi yahi idea hai — UDP ke upar TCP jaisi reliability.

Reliable UDP — packet 0, 1, 2 wali kahani

Game me har packet barabar zaroori nahi hota. Position wale packets kho jayein to chalega — agla packet nayi position le aayega. Par "shoot" jaisa packet kho jaye to dobara bhejna hi padega. Reliable UDP isi liye hai — zaroori packets ki guarantee, baaki sab fast. Dekho kaise:

  • Step 1 aur 2: Character A ne fire kiya. Packet 0 client ko mila. Client ne server ko acknowledge kiya.
  • Step 3: Character B ne fire kiya. Packet 1 raaste me kho gaya.
  • Step 4 aur 5: Character C ne fire kiya. Packet 2 client ko mila. Aakhri successfully delivered packet 0 tha, isliye client ko pata chal gaya ki packet 1 khoya hai — to packet 2 ko client ne buffer kar liya. Client ne packet 2 ka acknowledgement bhej diya.
  • Step 6 aur 7: Server ko packet 1 ka ack der tak nahi mila, to usne packet 1 dobara bhej diya. Packet 1 milte hi packet 1 aur 2 dono "delivered" ho gaye — ab kuch bhi buffer me nahi hai. Client ne packet 1 ka ack bhej diya.

Seekhne wali baat: receiver ko pata hota hai kaunsa packet khoya hai (sequence number se), isliye wo aage ke packets ko buffer karke rakhta hai, aur khoya hua packet dobara aane par sab kuch order me deliver kar deta hai. Isi liye game smooth chalta hai — na TCP wali delay, na UDP wali laparwahi.

TCP kahan use hota hai gaming me?

TCP bilkul bekaar nahi hai — game me bhi uski jagah hai: Login aur account: Password aur payment — yahan reliability chahiye, speed nahi. Chat messages: 'Hello' kho jaye to dobara bhejo — TCP theek hai. Game download aur updates: 50GB download me ek byte bhi kho jaye to file corrupt — TCP zaroori hai. Leaderboards aur matchmaking: HTTP APIs — TCP pe chalte hain.

Rule: Real-time gameplay = UDP. Baaki sab (login, chat, download) = TCP.

Lag, jitter aur packet loss — 3 dushman

Lag (latency): Packet ko jaane me kitna time — 20ms achha, 100ms+ kharab. Jitter: Latency me utaar-chadhav — kabhi 20ms, kabhi 200ms — game atak-atak ke chalta hai. Packet loss: Kitne packets kho gaye — 1% theek hai, 5%+ matlab game kharab.

Netcode: Games lag ko chhupane ke liye tricks use karte hain — client-side prediction (tumhara character turant badhta hai, server baad me confirm karta hai), lag compensation (server peeche jaake dekhta hai tumne kab shoot kiya tha), interpolation (do positions ke beech smooth movement dikhao).

3. Game packets — kya bheja jata hai?

DataProtocolKyun
Player position (har frame)UDP (unreliable)Nayi position har frame aati hai
Shoot / hitUDP (reliable)Kho jaye to game galat ho jayega
Player join/leaveUDP (reliable)Zaroori event hai
Login / paymentTCPReliability chahiye
ChatTCPMessage kho jaye to dobara bhejo
Game downloadTCPEk byte bhi nahi khona chahiye

4. Try karo — game khelo, TCP vs UDP

Ek shooting game khelo. Pehle TCP se, phir UDP se — dekho ek packet kho jaye to kya hota hai, aur kaunsa jeetta hai.

  1. 1. Game khelo — TCP se
    • → Tum aage badhe — packet bheja: position (10, 20)
    • → Packet KHO GAYA! TCP: 'Dobara bhejo!'
    • → Dobara bheja — 200ms lag gaye
    • → Tab tak tumhara character wahi khada raha — dushman ne shoot kar diya ✗
    • → Tum mar gaye — LAG ki wajah se
    • ✗ TCP GAME ME HAAR
  2. 2. Game khelo — UDP se
    • → Tum aage badhe — packet bheja: position (10, 20)
    • → Packet KHO GAYA! UDP: koi dobara nahi — agla packet bhej diya: position (12, 20)
    • → Character smooth aage badha — 1 frame ka glitch, pata bhi nahi chala
    • → Tumne shoot kiya — Zaroori packet (reliable UDP) — ACK mila ✓
    • → Tum jeet gaye! ✓
    • ✓ UDP GAME ME JEET
  3. 3. Shoot karo — reliable UDP
    • → Tumne shoot kiya — packet: 'SHOOT, target: enemy1'
    • → Packet kho gaya! Par ye zaroori packet hai — game ne dobara bheja
    • → Server ko mila → enemy1 mar gaya ✓
    • → Position packets kho jaye to chalega, par shoot ka packet dobara bhejna zaroori hai
    • → Yahi reliable UDP hai — zaroori cheez guarantee, baaki fast
  4. 4. Lag compensation dekho
    • → Tumhara ping: 100ms, dushman ka ping: 20ms
    • → Tumne dushman ko shoot kiya — tumhare screen pe wo wahan tha
    • → Server ne peeche jaake dekha: 100ms pehle dushman wahi tha ✓
    • → Hit count hua — fair game ✓
    • → Bina lag compensation ke high-ping players kabhi jeet nahi sakte

5. TCP vs UDP gaming me — ek table me

CheezTCPUDP
LatencyZyada (handshake + ACK + retransmit)Kam (bhejo aur bhool jao)
Packet lossDobara bhejta hai (delay)Ignore karta hai (agla packet aayega)
OrderGuaranteed (head-of-line blocking)Koi order nahi
Best forLogin, chat, downloadsReal-time gameplay

QUIC: UDP ke upar reliability + encryption — HTTP/3 aur kai naye games is taraf ja rahe hain.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Poora game TCP pe banana: Lag aur head-of-line blocking se game khelne layak nahi rahega. Gameplay ke liye UDP chahiye.
  2. UDP pe sab kuch unreliable maan lena: Shoot aur score jaise events reliable hone chahiye — UDP ke upar apna reliability layer banao.
  3. Latency ko ignore karna: Server location matter karta hai — Mumbai player ko Singapore server se behtar ping milega, US server se nahi. Region-wise servers rakho.
  4. Packet loss ko zero maan lena: Internet pe 1-2% loss normal hai — game ko loss handle karna aana chahiye (interpolation, prediction).
  5. Cheating ko bhoolna: Client pe bharosa mat karo — server authoritative hona chahiye (position, health, score server pe verify karo).

7. Interview corner

Q: Online gaming TCP use karta hai ya UDP?

UDP — kyunki game me latency sabse important hai. TCP me retransmission aur head-of-line blocking se delay hota hai. Games UDP ke upar apna reliability layer banate hain — zaroori packets (shoot, score) reliable, position updates unreliable.

Q: Reliable UDP kya hai?

UDP ke upar banaya gaya layer jo zaroori packets ko guarantee karta hai — sequence numbers, ACKs aur retransmission se. Position jaise packets unreliable rehte hain (agla packet aayega), par shoot/score jaise events dobara bheje jate hain.

Q: Lag compensation kya hai?

Server player ke ping ko dhyaan me rakh ke peeche jaake dekhta hai — 'jab isne shoot kiya tha, tab dushman kahan tha?' Isse high-ping players ko bhi fair chance milta hai.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Online gaming me UDP kyun use hota hai?

  • UDP me data kabhi nahi khota
  • UDP fast hai — low latency, khoya packet agle packet se cover ho jata hai ✓ Sahi jawab
  • UDP free hai
  • TCP gaming support nahi karta

Sawaal 2: Game me 'shoot' jaisa packet kaise bheja jata hai?

  • Normal UDP — kho jaye to chalega
  • Reliable UDP — dobara bhej ke guarantee karo ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Email se
  • TCP se hamesha
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Gaming = UDP (low latency) + custom reliability layer (zaroori events guarantee, position unreliable); TCP login/chat/download ke liye; lag compensation se high-ping players ko fair chance milta hai.
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-protocol-does-online-gaming-use-to-transmit-data.md
Pichla05 · DNS Record Types You Should KnowAgla07 · What is a Deadlock?
07Computer Fundamentals · Guide 07 / 12

What is a Deadlock?

Do log ek hi darwaze se ek saath nikalna chahte hain — dono ruk gaye, koi peeche nahi hat ta. Deadlock wahi hai: do ya zyada processes ek doosre ka intezaar karte rehte hain, aur koi bhi aage nahi badhta. System atak jata hai — aur iska hal samajhna OS interviews ka favourite hai.

1. Deadlock — ek lane wali sadak

Socho ek bahut patli sadak hai — ek hi gaadi nikal sakti hai. Do gaadiyan aamne-saamne aa gayi — dono aage badhna chahti hain, dono ruk gayi. Na koi peeche hate, na koi side de — deadlock. Dono ko kisi teesre (traffic police) ki zaroorat hai jo ek ko peeche hatne ko kahe.

Computer me wahi hota hai: Process A ke paas Resource 1 hai, use Resource 2 chahiye. Process B ke paas Resource 2 hai, use Resource 1 chahiye. Dono intezaar karte rehte hain — hamesha ke liye.

Deadlock ke 4 conditions (Coffman conditions): (1) Mutual Exclusion, (2) Hold and Wait, (3) No Preemption, (4) Circular Wait. Chaaron ek saath hon to hi deadlock hota hai — ek bhi tod do to deadlock nahi hoga.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

4 Conditions — ek-ek karke

1) Mutual Exclusion: Resource ek waqt pe sirf ek process use kar sakta hai (printer, lock). 2) Hold and Wait: Process ek resource pakde hue, doosre ka intezaar kar raha hai. 3) No Preemption: Resource zabardasti chheena nahi ja sakta — process khud chhode to hi milega. 4) Circular Wait: Processes ek circle me intezaar kar rahe hain — A → B → A.

Chaaron ek saath hon to deadlock possible hai (zaroori nahi — par risk hai). Koi ek condition tod do to deadlock impossible ho jata hai.

Real Example — database locks

Transaction A: Row 1 ko lock karta hai, phir Row 2 ko lock karna chahta hai. Transaction B: Row 2 ko lock karta hai, phir Row 1 ko lock karna chahta hai. Dono intezaar karte rehte hain — database atak gaya!

-- Transaction A:                -- Transaction B:
UPDATE accounts SET bal=bal-100   UPDATE accounts SET bal=bal-200
  WHERE id=1;  -- Row 1 lock        WHERE id=2;  -- Row 2 lock
UPDATE accounts SET bal=bal+100   UPDATE accounts SET bal=bal+200
  WHERE id=2;  -- Row 2 chahiye!     WHERE id=1;  -- Row 1 chahiye!
-- A Row 2 ka intezaar, B Row 1 ka — DEADLOCK!

Database kya karta hai? Deadlock detect karke ek transaction ko victim chun ke rollback kar deta hai — doosri aage badh jati hai. Victim ko dobara try karna padta hai.

Deadlock ko kaise handle karein? — 4 tareeke

1) Prevention: 4 conditions me se ek ko hone hi mat do — jaise saare locks ek fixed order me lo (hamesha Row 1 pehle, phir Row 2 — to circular wait kabhi nahi banega). Ya ek saath saare resources maango (hold-and-wait tod do).

2) Avoidance (Banker's Algorithm): Resource dene se pehle check karo — 'agar ye de diya to system safe state me rahega?' Safe nahi to ruko. Par iske liye pehle se pata hona chahiye har process ko kitne resources chahiye — practical nahi hai hamesha.

3) Detection + Recovery: Deadlock hone do, detect karo (wait-for graph me cycle dhoondho), phir ek process ko kill/rollback karke todo. Databases yehi karte hain.

4) Ignore (Ostrich Algorithm): Kuch OS (jaise Unix) deadlock ko ignore karte hain — 'kabhi-kabhi hoga, user restart kar lega'. Practical hai, kyunki deadlock rare hota hai.

Dining Philosophers — classic problem

5 philosophers ek table pe baithe hain, 5 chopsticks hain (har do ke beech ek). Har philosopher ko khane ke liye 2 chopsticks chahiye (left + right). Agar saare ek saath left chopstick utha lein to kisi ke paas right nahi bachegi — deadlock! Sab bhooke baithe rahenge.

Solutions: (1) Ek philosopher ko ulta kar do (pehle right uthaye) — circular wait toot jayega. (2) Ek saath sirf 4 philosophers ko baithne do. (3) Dono chopsticks ek saath uthao, warna ek bhi mat uthao.

Ye problem concurrency ka sabse famous example hai — interview me iska naam aate hi samajh jao deadlock ki baat ho rahi hai.

3. Deadlock vs Starvation vs Livelock

CheezKya hota haiFarq
DeadlockProcesses ek doosre ka intezaar karte hain, koi aage nahi badhtaSab atke hue hain
StarvationEk process ko kabhi resource nahi milta (doosre hamesha pehle le jate hain)Ek atka hai, baaki chal rahe hain
LivelockProcesses kaam kar rahe hain, par aage nahi badh rahe (ek doosre ko raasta dete rehte hain)Busy hain, par progress zero

Example: Do log ek patli gali me aamne-saamne — dono side hote rehte hain, par nikal nahi paate — ye livelock hai. Dono khade ho jayein aur hilna band kar dein — ye deadlock hai.

4. Try karo — deadlock banao aur todo

Do processes aur do resources hain. Pehle deadlock banao, phir use detect karo aur todo — alag-alag tareekon se.

  1. 1. Deadlock banao
    • → Process A: Resource 1 (Printer) lock kiya ✓
    • → Process B: Resource 2 (Scanner) lock kiya ✓
    • → Process A: 'Mujhe Resource 2 bhi chahiye' — intezaar...
    • → Process B: 'Mujhe Resource 1 bhi chahiye' — intezaar...
    • → A B ka intezaar, B A ka intezaar — CIRCULAR WAIT!
    • ✗ DEADLOCK — dono hamesha ke liye atke hue
  2. 2. Deadlock detect karo
    • → OS ne wait-for graph banaya: A → B, B → A
    • → Graph me CYCLE mila: A → B → A
    • → DEADLOCK DETECTED!
    • → Database hota to yahi karta hai — cycle dhoondhta hai, phir victim chunta hai
  3. 3. Recovery — ek ko rollback karo
    • → Victim chuna: Process B (kam kaam kiya tha, rollback sasta hai)
    • → Process B ko kill kiya — uske resources free hue
    • → Process A ko Resource 2 mil gaya → A aage badha ✓
    • → Process B ko dobara start kiya — is baar wo wait karega
    • ✓ DEADLOCK TOOTA — ek ko sacrifice karna pada
  4. 4. Prevention — fixed order me lock lo
    • → Naya rule: hamesha Resource 1 pehle, phir Resource 2 (fixed order)
    • → Process A: R1 → R2 ✓
    • → Process B: R1 maanga — A ke paas hai, intezaar karta hai
    • → A ka kaam khatam → resources free → B aage badha ✓
    • → Circular wait kabhi ban hi nahi sakta — kyunki order fixed hai
    • ✓ PREVENTION — deadlock hone hi nahi diya

5. Deadlock handle karne ke tareeke — ek table me

TareekaKaiseKahan use hota hai
Prevention4 conditions me se ek ko tod doFixed lock order (databases)
AvoidanceBanker's algorithm — safe state checkTheory, rare practical
Detection + RecoveryCycle dhoondho, victim ko rollback karoDatabases (PostgreSQL, MySQL)
Ignore (Ostrich)Kuch mat karo, restart kar loUnix/Linux OS

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Locks ko alag order me lena: Ek jagah R1→R2, doosri jagah R2→R1 — deadlock ka seedha raasta. Hamesha fixed order rakho.
  2. Lock ko zyada der pakde rakhna: Lock leke slow kaam (network call) karna — doosre processes intezaar karte rehte hain. Lock ko chhota rakho.
  3. Timeout na lagana: Lock ka intezaar hamesha ke liye mat karo — timeout pe wapas aao, dobara try karo (retry with backoff).
  4. Deadlock ko starvation samajhna: Starvation me ek process atka hai, baaki chal rahe hain. Deadlock me sab atke hain — hal alag hai.
  5. Nested locks bina soche: Ek lock ke andar doosra lock lena — har baar order check karo, warna deadlock pakka hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: Deadlock kya hai aur uski 4 conditions kaunsi hain?

Deadlock tab hota hai jab do ya zyada processes ek doosre ke resources ka intezaar karte rehte hain aur koi aage nahi badhta. 4 Coffman conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait — chaaron ek saath hon to hi deadlock hota hai.

Q: Deadlock ko kaise roka ja sakta hai?

Koi ek condition tod do — sabse common hai fixed lock order (circular wait tod do) ya saare resources ek saath maango (hold-and-wait tod do). Ya detection + recovery: cycle detect karke ek process ko rollback karo — databases yehi karte hain.

Q: Deadlock, starvation aur livelock me farq?

Deadlock me sab processes atke hain (circular wait). Starvation me ek process ko kabhi resource nahi milta, baaki chal rahe hain. Livelock me processes kaam kar rahe hain par progress zero hai — jaise do log gali me ek doosre ko raasta dete rehte hain.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Deadlock ke liye kitni conditions ek saath honi chahiye?

  • 1
  • 2
  • 4 — Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait ✓ Sahi jawab
  • 10

Sawaal 2: Fixed lock order se kaunsi condition tootti hai?

  • Mutual Exclusion
  • Circular Wait ✓ Sahi jawab
  • No Preemption
  • Hold and Wait
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Deadlock = processes ek doosre ka intezaar karte hain, koi aage nahi badhta; 4 Coffman conditions ek saath hon to hota hai; fixed lock order se roko, detection+recovery se todo; databases victim ko rollback karte hain.
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-is-a-deadlock.md
Pichla06 · TCP vs UDP for Online GamingAgla08 · Process vs Thread: Key Differences
08Computer Fundamentals · Guide 08 / 12

Process vs Thread: Key Differences

Har program chalta hai to wo process banta hai, aur har process ke andar threads hote hain. Dono kaam karte hain, par inke beech farq samajhna OS aur interviews, dono ke liye zaroori hai. Ek line me: process bhaari hai, thread halka hai.

1. Process vs Thread — ghar wali kahani

Process: Ek poora ghar hai — apni zameen (memory), apna saaman (resources), apne log (threads). Do ghar alag hain — ek ghar me aag lagi to doosra safe hai.

Thread: Ghar ke andar rehne wale log hain — sab ek hi ghar ka saaman share karte hain (kitchen, bathroom, memory). Ek ne kitchen ganda kiya to sabko dikhega. Log aana-jaana aasan hai (thread banana sasta hai), par ek ne kuch tod diya to poora ghar affect hoga.

Ek line me: Process = alag memory, alag resources, alag crash. Thread = shared memory, halka, fast — par ek crash hua to poora process gaya.

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Process kya hai?

Process ek running program hai — OS use alag memory (address space), file handles, aur resources deta hai. Har process ka apna PID hota hai.

Example: Chrome kholo to har tab ek alag process hota hai (Chrome ka design) — ek tab crash hua to doosre chalte rehte hain. Word aur Excel do alag processes hain.

Process banana mehenga hai: Nayi memory, naye resources, OS ko bahut kaam karna padta hai (fork + exec). Communication: Processes aapas me baat karne ke liye IPC chahiye (pipes, sockets, shared memory) — kyunki inki memory alag hai.

Thread kya hai?

Thread process ke andar ka execution unit hai — ek process me kai threads ho sakte hain, jo process ki memory aur resources share karte hain.

Example: Word me ek thread typing handle karta hai, doosra spell-check karta hai, teesra auto-save karta hai — teeno ek saath chalte hain, ek hi document (shared memory) pe.

Thread banana sasta hai: Nayi memory nahi chahiye — bas stack aur registers. Communication: Aasan — shared memory se seedha baat kar sakte hain. Par iska khatra bhi hai: race condition — do threads ek hi data ko ek saath badal dein to gadbad ho jati hai. Isliye locks/mutex chahiye.

Context switching — kaunsa bhaari hai?

Process switch: Poori memory map badalni padti hai, TLB flush karna padta hai, cache khaali ho jata hai — slow (microseconds se milliseconds).

Thread switch: Sirf registers aur stack badlo — memory wahi rehti hai — fast (nanoseconds se microseconds).

Isi liye servers har request ke liye naya process nahi, thread pool use karte hain — threads pehle se bane hote hain, request aate hi kaam shuru.

Kab process, kab thread?

Process chuno jab: Isolation chahiye (ek crash hua to doosra safe rahe — Chrome tabs), security chahiye (alag user/permissions), ya alag program chalana ho.

Thread chuno jab: Shared data pe kaam hai (ek hi document), speed chahiye (fast switching), ya kai chhote kaam parallel karne hain (web server har request pe thread).

Modern approach: Dono ka combination — kai processes, har ek me kai threads. Aur aaj kal async/event-loop (Node.js) bhi hai — bina threads ke bhi concurrency, par wo alag kahani hai.

3. Side-by-side comparison

CheezProcessThread
MemoryAlag (own address space)Shared (process ki memory)
BananaMehenga (slow)Sasta (fast)
SwitchingSlow (TLB flush)Fast
CommunicationIPC chahiye (pipe/socket)Shared memory (seedha)
CrashDoosre processes safePoora process crash
ResourcesApne (files, handles)Process ke share karte hain
ExampleChrome tab, Word, ExcelWord me typing + spell-check
# Python me process vs thread
import threading, multiprocessing

# Thread — shared memory, fast
t = threading.Thread(target=kaam_karo)
t.start()

# Process — alag memory, isolation
p = multiprocessing.Process(target=kaam_karo)
p.start()
# Note: Python me GIL ki wajah se threads CPU kaam parallel nahi karte —
# CPU-bound kaam ke liye processes, I/O-bound ke liye threads behtar hain.

4. Try karo — process aur thread banao

Ek web server banao: pehle har request pe naya process, phir thread pool — dekho speed aur memory me kya farq padta hai.

  1. 1. Naya process banao
    • → $ ./myapp — OS ne naya process banaya (PID 1234)
    • → Memory allocate hui: 50MB alag address space
    • → Time laga: ~5ms (fork + exec + memory setup)
    • → Process crash hua to doosre processes safe ✓
    • → Par har request pe naya process = bahut slow aur bhaari
  2. 2. Naya thread banao
    • → Process ke andar thread banaya — memory share ki, nayi nahi li
    • → Time laga: ~0.05ms (100x fast!)
    • → Thread ne shared data padha — seedha, bina IPC ke ✓
    • → Par: thread crash hua to poora process crash ✗
    • → Race condition: do threads ne ek hi counter badaya — galat jawab!
  3. 3. Race condition dekho
    • → Counter = 100. Thread A: counter+1, Thread B: counter+1
    • → Dono ne ek saath 100 padha, dono ne 101 likha
    • → Final counter: 101 — hona chahiye tha 102! ✗
    • → Fix: mutex lock lagao — ek waqt pe ek hi thread counter badle
    • → Lock ke saath: counter = 102 ✓ — sahi, par thoda slow
  4. 4. Web server — thread pool
    • → 100 requests aayi — har ek pe naya thread banaya to 100 threads, memory khatam
    • → Thread pool: pehle se 10 threads bane hue hain
    • → Request aayi → khaali thread ko do → kaam khatam → thread wapas pool me
    • → Fast + memory control me ✓ — yahi production servers karte hain

5. Program, Process, Thread — teeno ka rishta

CheezKya haiExample
ProgramDisk pe pada code (passive)chrome.exe file
ProcessChalta hua program (active)Chrome chal raha hai (PID 1234)
ThreadProcess ke andar kaam karne wala unitChrome tab ka renderer thread

Yaad rakhna: Ek program → kai processes. Ek process → kai threads. Thread process ke bina nahi reh sakta — process khatam hua to uske saare threads bhi khatam.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Har kaam ke liye naya process banana: Mehenga hai — threads ya thread pool use karo.
  2. Shared data ko bina lock ke badalna: Race condition — do threads ek hi data badal dein to result galat hoga. Mutex/lock lagao.
  3. Thread ko process samajhna: Thread ka apna memory nahi hota — wo process ki memory share karta hai. Thread crash = process crash.
  4. Python me threads se CPU kaam parallel karne ki koshish: GIL ki wajah se Python threads CPU-bound kaam parallel nahi karte — multiprocessing use karo.
  5. Thread leak: Threads bana ke band na karna — hazaar threads memory kha jayenge. Thread pool use karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: Process aur thread me farq kya hai?

Process ek running program hai — uski alag memory aur resources hote hain, banana mehenga hai, crash hua to doosre processes safe rehte hain. Thread process ke andar ka execution unit hai — memory share karta hai, banana sasta aur switching fast hai, par crash hua to poora process gaya.

Q: Thread switching process switching se fast kyun hai?

Kyunki thread switch me sirf registers aur stack badalte hain — memory map wahi rehta hai. Process switch me poori memory map badalni padti hai aur TLB flush karna padta hai — jo slow hai.

Q: Race condition kya hai?

Jab do threads shared data ko ek saath badalte hain aur final result galat ho jata hai — jaise counter 100 se 102 hona chahiye tha, par 101 ho gaya. Fix: mutex/lock se ek waqt pe ek hi thread ko data badalne do.

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: Process aur thread me main farq kya hai?

  • Koi farq nahi
  • Process ki alag memory hoti hai, thread process ki memory share karta hai ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Thread bada hota hai
  • Process fast hota hai

Sawaal 2: Race condition kab hoti hai?

  • Jab ek thread kaam kare
  • Jab do threads shared data ko ek saath badlein bina lock ke ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Jab process crash ho
  • Jab RAM full ho
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Program = disk pe code; Process = chalta hua program, alag memory, mehenga; Thread = process ke andar kaam karne wala, shared memory, sasta aur fast; shared data pe lock lagao (race condition se bacho).
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-is-the-difference-between-process-and-thread.md
Pichla07 · What is a Deadlock?Agla09 · OSI Model Explained
09Computer Fundamentals · Guide 09 / 12

OSI Model Explained

Jab tum website kholte ho, to data 7 paraton (layers) se hokar guzarta hai — har parat ka apna kaam hai. OSI Model network communication ko samajhne ka standard tareeka hai. Interview me 'OSI ke 7 layers batao' — ye sawaal lagbhag pakka aata hai.

1. OSI — parcel bhejne wali kahani

Socho tum ek parcel bhej rahe ho: (7) Tum letter likhte ho (Application). (6) Use ek lifafe me daalte ho, sahi format me (Presentation). (5) Courier se baat karte ho — 'parcel bhej do, tracking chahiye' (Session). (4) Parcel ko tukdon me baant te ho, har tukde pe number likhte ho (Transport). (3) Har tukde pe address likhte ho (Network). (2) Tukdon ko truck me load karte ho, padosi truck se takra na jaye (Data Link). (1) Truck sadak pe chalta hai (Physical).

Paane wala ulta order me kholta hai: sadak → truck → address → tukde jodna → courier → lifafa → letter. Har parat sirf apne kaam se matlab rakhti hai — upar wali parat ko neeche ka pata nahi.

Yaad rakhne ka tareeka: 'Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away' — Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application (neeche se upar).

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Layer 7-5 — Application, Presentation, Session

7) Application: User se seedha matlab — HTTP (web), SMTP (email), FTP (files), DNS. Tum jo app use karte ho, wo yahan hai.

6) Presentation: Data ka format — encryption (TLS), compression, character encoding (UTF-8). Data ko aise badlo ki dono taraf samajh aaye.

5) Session: Connection ko manage karna — session shuru karna, maintain karna, band karna. Login session, video call ka session — yahan ka kaam hai.

Internet pe asal me ye teen layers aksar ek saath implement hoti hain (application me hi) — par samajhne ke liye alag rakhi gayi hain.

Layer 4 — Transport (TCP/UDP)

Transport layer end-to-end delivery ki zimmedari leta hai: data ko segments me baantna, port numbers se sahi app tak pahunchana, aur reliability dena.

TCP: Reliable — order, retransmission, flow control. Web, email, file transfer. UDP: Fast, unreliable — video, gaming, DNS.

Port: Har app ka number — HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, SSH 22. Transport layer port dekh ke decide karta hai packet kis app ko dena hai.

Layer 3 — Network (IP, Routing)

Network layer ka kaam hai packet ko sahi address (IP) tak pahunchana — chahe wo duniya ke doosre kone me ho. Routers yahan kaam karte hain.

IP: Har device ka address. Routing: Sabse achha raasta chunna — BGP, OSPF protocols. Packet har router pe ek hop aage badhta hai, jab tak destination na mil jaye.

Logical addressing (IP) yahan hoti hai — physical addressing (MAC) neeche wali layer me.

Layer 2-1 — Data Link aur Physical

2) Data Link: Ek hi network ke andar delivery — MAC address (hardware address) se. Switch yahan kaam karta hai. Data ko frames me baanta jata hai, error detection (CRC) hoti hai.

1) Physical: Asli signals — cable, Wi-Fi radio waves, light (fiber). Bits ko 0/1 se electrical/optical signal me badalna. Hub, repeater, cables — sab yahan hain.

Devices: Hub/Repeater → Layer 1, Switch → Layer 2, Router → Layer 3, Firewall → Layer 3/4/7 (kuch bhi ho sakta hai).

3. 7 Layers — ek table me

#LayerKaamExample / Device
7ApplicationUser ko service denaHTTP, SMTP, DNS
6PresentationFormat, encryption, compressionTLS, JPEG, UTF-8
5SessionConnection manage karnaLogin session, NetBIOS
4TransportEnd-to-end delivery, portsTCP, UDP
3NetworkRouting, IP addressingIP, Router
2Data LinkEk network me delivery, MACEthernet, Switch
1PhysicalSignals, cablesFiber, Wi-Fi, Hub

Data ka naam har layer pe: Layer 7-5: Data → Layer 4: Segment → Layer 3: Packet → Layer 2: Frame → Layer 1: Bits. Har layer apna header jodti hai (encapsulation) — paane wala har layer pe header kholta hai (de-encapsulation).

4. Try karo — ek message 7 layers se bhejo

'Hello' message bhejo aur dekho har layer usme kya jodti hai — phir paane wale ki taraf se har layer use kaise kholti hai.

  1. 1. Message likho — Layer 7
    • → Tumne likha: 'Hello' (Application layer — HTTP request)
    • → Browser ne HTTP request banayi: GET /hello
    • → Layer 7 ka kaam poora — ab neeche bhejo
  2. 2. Encrypt aur format karo — Layer 6-5
    • → Layer 6 (Presentation): TLS se encrypt kiya — 'Hello' → encrypted kachra
    • → Layer 5 (Session): session establish kiya — connection ID 42
    • → Ab data encrypted hai aur session bana hua hai
  3. 3. Segments banao — Layer 4
    • → Layer 4 (Transport): data ko segments me kaata, port lagaya (443)
    • → TCP ne sequence number diya: Segment 1, Seq 1000
    • → Port 443 = HTTPS — sahi app ko milega ✓
  4. 4. Address lagao — Layer 3
    • → Layer 3 (Network): IP header joda — Source: tumhara IP, Destination: 142.250.80.46
    • → Packet ban gaya — router ko pata hai kahan bhejna hai
    • → Router ne raasta chuna: Delhi → Mumbai → Singapore → Google
  5. 5. Frame banao — Layer 2
    • → Layer 2 (Data Link): MAC address joda — agle router ka MAC
    • → Frame ban gaya + error check (CRC) lagaya
    • → Switch ne frame ko sahi port se aage bhej diya
  6. 6. Signals bhejo — Layer 1
    • → Layer 1 (Physical): bits ko electrical signals me badla
    • → Fiber optic cable se light ki speed se gaya! ⚡
    • → Har hop pe: Physical → Data Link → Network → ... dobara neeche
    • → Destination pe ulta: Physical se upar, har layer header kholti hai
    • → Aakhir me: 'Hello' — waapas plain text me! ✓

5. OSI vs TCP/IP model

OSI (7 layers)TCP/IP (4 layers)
Application, Presentation, SessionApplication (teeno ek me)
TransportTransport
NetworkInternet
Data Link, PhysicalNetwork Access (dono ek me)

Farq: OSI ek theoretical model hai (samajhne ke liye), TCP/IP asal me use hota hai (internet pe). Interview me dono ka farq poochte hain — OSI 7 layers, TCP/IP 4 layers.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. Layers ka order ulta yaad karna: Mnemonic use karo: 'Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away' (neeche se upar).
  2. OSI ko asal protocol samajhna: OSI ek model hai — internet TCP/IP model pe chalta hai. OSI samajhne ke liye hai, implement karne ke liye nahi.
  3. Router aur Switch ko mix karna: Router Layer 3 (IP routing), Switch Layer 2 (MAC) — alag kaam, alag layer.
  4. TLS ko galat layer me rakhna: TLS Presentation layer (6) me aata hai — Application (HTTP) ke neeche, Transport (TCP) ke upar.
  5. Encapsulation bhoolna: Har layer apna header jodti hai — data ka naam badalta hai: Data → Segment → Packet → Frame → Bits.

7. Interview corner

Q: OSI model ke 7 layers batao.

Neeche se upar: Physical (signals/cables), Data Link (MAC, frames, switch), Network (IP, routing, router), Transport (TCP/UDP, ports), Session (connection management), Presentation (encryption/compression/format), Application (HTTP, SMTP, DNS).

Q: OSI aur TCP/IP model me farq?

OSI 7 layers ka theoretical model hai — samajhne ke liye. TCP/IP 4 layers ka practical model hai — internet asal me ispe chalta hai. TCP/IP me Application layer OSI ki top 3 layers ko mila deti hai.

Q: Router kis layer pe kaam karta hai?

Layer 3 (Network) — IP address dekh ke packet ko sahi raaste pe bhejta hai. Switch Layer 2 pe (MAC address), Hub Layer 1 pe (sirf signals repeat karta hai).

8. Quick check

Sawaal 1: OSI model me Transport layer (Layer 4) ka main kaam kya hai?

  • IP address dena
  • End-to-end delivery — TCP/UDP, ports, reliability ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Cables bichhana
  • Website dikhana

Sawaal 2: Router OSI ki kis layer pe kaam karta hai?

  • Layer 2
  • Layer 3 (Network) ✓ Sahi jawab
  • Layer 7
  • Layer 1
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: OSI = 7 layers: Physical → Data Link → Network → Transport → Session → Presentation → Application; har layer ka apna kaam; data neeche jaate waqt header judta hai (encapsulation), upar aate waqt khulta hai.
Sourcehttps://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/what-is-osi-model.md
Pichla08 · Process vs Thread: Key DifferencesAgla10 · Visualizing a SQL Query
10Computer Fundamentals · Guide 10 / 12

Visualizing a SQL Query

Tum SELECT likhte ho aur jawab mil jata hai — par database ke andar kya hota hai? SQL query likhne ka order aur chalne ka order alag hota hai! Is page me ek query ko step-by-step visualize karo — kaunsa clause pehle chalta hai, kaunsa aakhir me, aur kyun.

1. SQL query — khana banane wali kahani

Socho tum khana bana rahe ho. Recipe me likha hai: 'Paneer Butter Masala banao' — par kaam ka order hai: (1) Sabzi kharido (FROM), (2) Kharab wali nikalo (WHERE), (3) Kaato aur group karo (GROUP BY), (4) Masale daalo (HAVING), (5) Plate me sajao (SELECT), (6) Upar se dhaniya daalo (ORDER BY), (7) Sirf 2 plate serve karo (LIMIT).

SQL me bhi likhne ka order aur chalne ka order alag hai: tum SELECT pehle likhte ho, par database use lagbhag aakhir me chalata hai. Isi liye WHERE me tum SELECT me banaye hue alias ko use nahi kar sakte — wo abhi bana hi nahi!

Logical order: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT. Likhne ka order: SELECT → FROM → WHERE → ... — bilkul ulta shuru hota hai!

2. Gehrai me samjho — ek-ek point

Step 1-2 — FROM aur WHERE

FROM: Sabse pehle database tables ko jodta hai (JOIN) — poora data ikattha karta hai. FROM orders JOIN customers matlab dono tables ka combined data.

WHERE: Phir rows ko filter karta hai — ek-ek row ko check karta hai. WHERE amount > 1000 — sirf wahi rows aage badhengi jinki amount 1000 se zyada hai.

Important: WHERE row-level filter hai — ye GROUP BY se pehle chalta hai. Isliye WHERE me aggregate functions (SUM, COUNT) use nahi kar sakte — wo abhi bane hi nahi.

Step 3-4 — GROUP BY aur HAVING

GROUP BY: Bachi hui rows ko groups me baant ta hai — jaise har customer ke orders ek group me. GROUP BY customer_id — har customer ek group.

HAVING: Groups ko filter karta hai — group-level filter. HAVING SUM(amount) > 5000 — sirf wahi customers jinki total kharid 5000 se zyada hai.

WHERE vs HAVING: WHERE rows ko filter karta hai (GROUP BY se pehle), HAVING groups ko filter karta hai (GROUP BY ke baad). Dono ka kaam alag hai — mix mat karo.

Step 5-6 — SELECT aur DISTINCT

SELECT: Ab aake columns chunte hain — kaunse columns dikhane hain, kaunse calculations karne hain. SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total — yahan total alias banta hai.

Isi liye: WHERE me total alias use nahi kar sakte — SELECT abhi chala hi nahi tha! Par ORDER BY me use kar sakte ho — kyunki ORDER BY SELECT ke baad chalta hai.

DISTINCT: Duplicate rows hatata hai — SELECT ke baad chalta hai.

Step 7-8 — ORDER BY aur LIMIT

ORDER BY: Result ko sort karta hai — ORDER BY total DESC — sabse zyada kharch karne wala pehle. Yahan SELECT ke alias use kar sakte ho.

LIMIT/OFFSET: Aakhir me sirf utni rows do jitni maangi — LIMIT 10 — top 10 customers. Pagination isi se hoti hai.

Execution order ka fayda: Query optimize karte waqt samajh aata hai kahan time lag raha hai — WHERE pe index lagao (pehle filter), SELECT me sirf zaroori columns lo (kam data).

3. Ek query, poora flow — visualize karo

-- Tum likhte ho (likhne ka order):
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM orders
WHERE amount > 1000
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(amount) > 5000
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- Database chalata hai (logical order):
1. FROM orders               → 1,00,000 rows
2. WHERE amount > 1000        → 40,000 rows bachi
3. GROUP BY customer_id       → 5,000 groups bane
4. HAVING SUM(amount) > 5000  → 500 groups bache
5. SELECT customer_id, SUM()  → 500 rows, alias 'total' bana
6. ORDER BY total DESC        → sort hua
7. LIMIT 5                    → top 5 rows mili — JAWAAB!

-- EXPLAIN se dekho database kya kar raha hai:
-- EXPLAIN SELECT ... → execution plan dikhata hai:
-- kaunsa index use hua, kitni rows scan hui, kahan time laga

4. Try karo — ek query ko step-by-step chalao

Ek orders table hai (1,00,000 rows). Query chalao aur dekho har step pe kitni rows bachti hain — aur kahan index madad karta hai.

  1. 1. FROM — saara data lao
    • → FROM orders: 1,00,000 rows load hui
    • → JOIN hota to aur bhi zyada — pehle tables judti hain
    • → Abhi tak koi filter nahi — poora data hai
  2. 2. WHERE — rows filter karo
    • → WHERE amount > 1000: 1,00,000 → 40,000 rows
    • → Index hai amount pe? Haan to database seedha wahi rows nikalta hai (fast)
    • → Index nahi hai to poori table scan karni padegi (slow — full table scan!)
    • → Lesson: WHERE wale columns pe index lagao
  3. 3. GROUP BY + HAVING — groups banao
    • → GROUP BY customer_id: 40,000 rows → 5,000 groups
    • → HAVING SUM(amount) > 5000: 5,000 → 500 groups
    • → WHERE rows ko filter karta hai, HAVING groups ko — farq yaad rakho!
  4. 4. SELECT + ORDER BY + LIMIT
    • → SELECT: 500 rows me se columns chune — customer_id, total
    • → ORDER BY total DESC: sort hua (500 rows sort karna aasan hai)
    • → LIMIT 5: top 5 mile — JAWAAB TAYYAR ✓
    • → Total time: index ki wajah se 50ms — bina index ke 5 second lagte!
  5. 5. Galti karo — WHERE me alias use karo
    • → Query: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total ... WHERE total > 5000
    • → ERROR! 'Unknown column total' ✗
    • → Kyun? WHERE SELECT se pehle chalta hai — alias 'total' abhi bana hi nahi!
    • → Fix: HAVING SUM(amount) > 5000 use karo — HAVING GROUP BY ke baad chalta hai ✓

5. Logical order — ek table me

OrderClauseKaam
1FROM / JOINTables jodo, data ikattha karo
2WHERERows filter karo (row-level)
3GROUP BYRows ko groups me baanto
4HAVINGGroups filter karo (group-level)
5SELECTColumns chuno, alias banao
6DISTINCTDuplicates hatao
7ORDER BYSort karo
8LIMIT / OFFSETSirf utni rows do

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  1. WHERE me SELECT alias use karna: WHERE SELECT se pehle chalta hai — alias abhi bana hi nahi. HAVING ya subquery use karo.
  2. WHERE me aggregate function use karna: WHERE SUM(amount) > 5000 — galat hai. Aggregate ke liye HAVING use karo.
  3. SELECT * likhna: Saare columns laana slow hai — sirf zaroori columns lo, khaas karke badi tables me.
  4. WHERE wale column pe index na hona: Bina index ke full table scan hota hai — 1 lakh rows scan karna slow hai. EXPLAIN se check karo.
  5. ORDER BY + LIMIT ke bina pagination: Bina ORDER BY ke LIMIT ka result random order me aayega — har baar alag rows milengi.

7. Interview corner

Q: SQL query ka logical order kya hai?

FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT. Likhne ka order SELECT se shuru hota hai, par chalne ka order FROM se. Isi liye WHERE me SELECT alias use nahi kar sakte.

Q: WHERE aur HAVING me farq?
